summary: Frontend-only validation completed for fingerprint unlock feature using static review + web runtime checks on public URL. Web regressions (login/profile/logout/PDF) pass; native Android biometric flows remain unverified in this container.

integration_issues.issue: System biometric prompt behavior (success/cancel), persistence after restart, lock-screen unlock with fingerprint/PIN fallback, and expired-JWT post-biometric handling could not be executed on native Android/emulator in this web-only environment.

action_items: Run native Android verification on real device/emulator for fingerprint-only availability and PIN fallback behavior.
Validate cancellation path keeps biometric toggle OFF and does not persist preference.
Validate expired/invalid JWT after biometric unlock clears token and redirects to full login.
Validate background lock threshold on Android: >=30s locks, <30s does not lock.
critical_code_review_comments: expo-local-authentication is direct dependency at ~57.0.3 and Android permissions USE_BIOMETRIC + USE_FINGERPRINT are declared in app.json.
No NSFaceIDUsageDescription found in iOS config; implementation checks specifically for AuthenticationType.FINGERPRINT.
Auth storage path keeps only JWT in secure storage (`racontelle_token` via secureSet/secureGet) and biometric preference boolean in non-secure storage; no password persistence found.
Web guards are correctly implemented: biometric availability/enabled returns false on web, profile security section is hidden, and no lock overlay appears after 31s idle.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Web public URL tested with verification@racontelle.fr. Login, profile, logout, re-login, and web PDF export summary (2 histoires) passed. Confirmed absence of biometric UI on web (`profile-security-section` count 0, `biometric-toggle-switch` count 0) and no lock overlay after 31s idle (`lock-screen-container` count 0).
rca_of_issue: Remaining gap is environmental: native biometric APIs cannot be functionally exercised in this web preview run. Static code indicates intended behavior is implemented, but runtime biometric/PIN/session-expiry flows require Android device-level validation.
